summary: All models run and are reproducible. Four carry honest caveats (low-data classifiers, synthetic-data optimism, and simulated-data label leakage) that are reported here rather than hidden.

findings.finding: Real RandomForest/LogReg trained with a Dummy baseline; accuracy sits near the base rate due to class imbalance, which the module reports honestly.
findings.action: Interpret with ROC/PR-AUC, not accuracy. No change needed.

findings.finding: Single-split accuracy 0.75 on a very small labelled set; rare classes (e.g. 'engagement') have almost no support.
findings.action: Cross-validated weighted-F1: 0.763 ± 0.091 (weighted-F1, 5-fold). Grow the labelled set and report CV, not a single split.

findings.finding: Single-split accuracy 1.0 — 1.0 on ~24 test rows is an overfit red flag, not real perfection.
findings.action: Cross-validated weighted-F1: 0.903 ± 0.073 (weighted-F1, 5-fold). Treat as a low-data classifier; report CV with confidence intervals.

findings.finding: High R² on the engagement dataset (RandomForest R²=0.989, MAE=0.0188). On a synthetic/semi-simulated corpus this is likely optimistic.
findings.action: Report engagement prediction as a relative ranker, not an absolute predictor; validate on real platform exports via learning/ loop.

findings.finding: Simulated AUC ≈ 1.0 is inflated by label leakage (targets are defined by the same events used as features).
findings.action: The honest number is the real-data (UCI Bank-Marketing) validation AUC ≈ 0.9535. Report that, and label simulated metrics clearly.
